title: Raise daily transfer limit for Premium customers to €5,000
requestSummary: Premium customers should have their daily transfer limit raised from €1,000 to €5,000. Standard customers remain at €1,000. Currently both tiers share a single DAILY_LIMIT = 1000 constant with no tier-awareness in either repository.
openQuestions: Should the fraud review threshold (€2,000 in fraud/rules.ts) be raised or made tier-aware for Premium customers who can now legitimately transfer up to €5,000?
What is the new /api/limits response contract: return { standard, premium } or accept a customerId query param?
How should the mobile app receive the customer's tier — passed in TransferPayload, fetched from getAccount(), or stored in app state?
Should the analytics events (trackLimitReached, trackTransferInitiated) include a tier field for segmentation?

entryPoints.label: POST /api/transfers (novabank-api)
entryPoints.description: Main HTTP entry point for initiating a transfer. Calls executeTransfer() which enforces the daily limit. Both tiers use the same DAILY_LIMIT constant today.

entryPoints.label: GET /api/limits (novabank-api)
entryPoints.description: Returns the current daily limit. Currently returns { dailyLimit: 1000 } regardless of tier. Consumed by novabank-mobile getLimits().

entryPoints.label: TransferScreen.submitTransfer() (novabank-mobile)
entryPoints.description: Mobile entry point that shows the daily-limit label and calls client-side validateTransfer() before calling postTransfer(). Both label and validation are hardcoded to €1,000.

simulations.rawOutput: 3 existing suite tests broken by naive one-line bump. Standard customers' limit silently raised. Tier-aware implementation required.

effortEstimate: 4–6 h backend (novabank-api) + 2–3 h mobile (novabank-mobile), ~80 lines changed
riskRationale: The change requires a non-trivial architectural addition (tier-aware limit lookup) across two repositories and an API contract change. The fraud threshold (€2,000) is a hard blocker: without Compliance sign-off, Premium customers above €2,000 will be stuck in manual review. A naive one-line fix breaks 3 existing tests and silently removes Standard customers' protection. The notifications template has 0% coverage, creating a hidden regression risk.

blockedBy.reason: The existing fraud review threshold (€2,000 in fraud/rules.ts) will flag every Premium transfer above €2,000 as PENDING_REVIEW. Business must decide whether to raise or tier the fraud threshold before the feature can go live for Premium customers.

changePlan.action: Obtain Compliance/Fraud team sign-off on the €2,000 fraud review threshold for Premium customers
changePlan.rationale: Fraud rules.ts flags all transfers above €2,000 as PENDING_REVIEW. Without a decision here, Premium transfers €2,001–€5,000 will queue for manual review, effectively negating the feature.

changePlan.action: Split DAILY_LIMIT into DAILY_LIMIT_STANDARD = 1000 and DAILY_LIMIT_PREMIUM = 5000, and add getLimitForTier(tier: CustomerTier): number in src/transfers/limits.ts
changePlan.rationale: This is the authoritative source of the business rule. Splitting avoids silently raising Standard customers' limit.

changePlan.action: Update executeTransfer() in transferService.ts to fetch the customer record before the limit check and call getLimitForTier(customer.tier) instead of DAILY_LIMIT
changePlan.rationale: The service is the enforcement point. It already loads the DB; adding tier lookup is a minimal change. Add error path for missing customer.

changePlan.action: Update GET /api/limits in routes.ts to return { standard: 1000, premium: 5000 } — agree contract with mobile team before merging
changePlan.rationale: The mobile app's getLimits() function and the route test both depend on this shape. Changing the shape requires coordinated updates in both repos.

changePlan.action: Update limitInfo() in notifications/templates.ts to accept a CustomerTier parameter and add test coverage (currently 0%)
changePlan.rationale: Notifications will show the wrong limit to Premium customers without this fix. The 0% coverage means regressions here are invisible.

changePlan.action: Update tests/limits.test.ts, tests/transferService.test.ts, and tests/routes.test.ts to cover both tiers
changePlan.rationale: Three existing tests break on the naive fix. New Premium scenarios must be added: accept €3,000, reject €5,500; confirm Standard still rejected at €1,100.

changePlan.action: Replace CLIENT_DAILY_LIMIT constant in validateTransfer.ts with a tierLimit parameter: validateTransfer(amount: number, tierLimit: number)
changePlan.rationale: The client-side guard must mirror the server-side tier logic. Passing the limit as a parameter removes the hardcoded constant and makes the function testable per tier.

changePlan.action: Update TransferScreen.submitTransfer() to call getLimits() on invocation, display the dynamic label, and pass the limit to validateTransfer()
changePlan.rationale: getLimits() already exists in api.ts but is never called from the app (dead code). Wiring it here completes the intended integration and removes the hardcoded '€1,000' label.

changePlan.action: Update tests/TransferScreen.test.ts and tests/api.test.ts to cover Standard and Premium tier scenarios
changePlan.rationale: Current tests assert '1,000' in label and reject 1500 (valid for Premium). Both must become tier-parameterised to prevent regressions.

changePlan.action: (Optional) Add tier field to trackLimitReached() and trackTransferInitiated() in analytics/events.ts
changePlan.rationale: Without tier in analytics events, the business cannot segment 'limit reached' metrics by customer tier after the feature ships.
